core_obligations: Reduction to $Y$ scheme: for $(X_U \to U, \mathcal{L}_U)$ get the open $V' \subset U$; the functorial characterization gives $s^{-1}(V') = t^{-1}(V')$ on $R = U \times_Y U$, descending to an open subspace $V \subset Y$ with $V'$ its inverse image; relative ampleness of $\mathcal{L}_V$ on $X_V/V$ follows by \'etale locality, and any $Y'$ with ample pullback factors through $V$ (proof lines 2440-2470).
Reduce the affine case to point (A): ampleness at one fibre spreads to a neighbourhood; by the delivered fpqc locality of ampleness assume $k = \kappa(y)$ (proof lines 2470-2477).

Limit approximation: write $X \to Y = \lim (X_i \to Y_i)$ over $\mathbf{Z}$ with affine transitions (Limits of Spaces lemma), shrink so $Y_i$ are affine schemes, descend $\mathcal{L}$ to compatible $\mathcal{L}_i$, and shrink so $X_{i, y_i}$ are schemes (proof lines 2479-2500).

Spread: for some $i$, $\mathcal{L}_{i, y_i}$ is ample (limit-ample lemma); the Divisors on Spaces neighbourhood lemma gives $V_i \subset Y_i$; $V = $ inverse image of $V_i$ works by the hinted composition (ample base change; $X \to Y \times_{Y_i} X_i$ affine; ampleness preserved under affine pullback) (proof lines 2500-2513).
proof_roadmap: Descend the open from an \'etale chart through the groupoid relation.
Reduce the affine case to spreading from one fibre.
Approximate by finite-presentation models and descend the line bundle.
Spread ampleness on the model and pull it back along the affine morphism.
difficulty_reason: Two deep arguments in sequence: (i) reduction to $Y$ scheme via the groupoid chart $R = U \times_Y U$, where the functorial characterization forces $s^{-1}(V') = t^{-1}(V')$, descending the open to $Y$; (ii) the affine case by limit approximation: an inverse system of finite-presentation models over $\mathbf{Z}$ with affine transitions, descent of the invertible module, scheme-ness of the fibres after shrinking, ample spreading on the model (limits + Divisors lemmas), and the final pullback along the affine morphism $X \to Y \times_{Y_i} X_i$ (ingredients named by the author as hints).
